quotes.text: Conditional access decides who may try. A policy gate decides what may happen. Treat one as necessary the other as non-negotiable.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Crisp distinction between token-time and action-time control for agents.

quotes.text: Audit tells you what happened. Provenance tells you why you think it happened. A policy gate decides whether it's allowed to happen at all.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable framework separating forensics, explanation and prevention.

quotes.text: If an event can't be safely replayed, it shouldn't control state. That applies to deletes, emails, shares, payments and anything with a blast radius.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical design rule for event-driven agent workflows.

quotes.text: If a chunk is not eligible for this actor, in this venue, at this moment, it does not exist. Eligibility is computed before similarity, not after generation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes retrieval as an authorization event rather than a search feature.

quotes.text: Least privilege is not only about breadth, it's also about time. The right to act should be the exception, not the baseline.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear recommendation for time-bound agent permissions.

Experience plane tax and NHIs as super users

takeaways: Conditional Access and Purview audit are necessary but act at token time and after the fact, so high-risk agent tool calls need a deterministic per-call policy gate.
Treat events as proposals, not state: idempotency keys, an authoritative state store and segmented read, write and egress identities keep agent failures small.
Retrieval should be an authorization boundary with venue-aware filtering, cite-or-silent generation and persisted policy outcomes as proof.
hook: Giving AI agents a face and a voice makes them feel trustworthy, but it does nothing to stop a mis-scoped delete or an overshared answer. This episode is for Microsoft 365 architects and security leaders deploying agents with Entra Agent ID, Copilot Studio and Purview. Learn how per-tool policy gates, segmented identities and retrieval boundaries turn eloquent outages into denied decisions.
